title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 51-52
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 51 to 52 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'धर्मगुब्धर्मकृद्धर्मी सदसत्क्षरमक्षरम्'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 51 to 52 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 51 to 52.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 51 to 52** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **धर्मगुब्धर्मकृद्धर्मी सदसत्क्षरमक्षरम्**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**धर्मगुब्धर्मकृद्धर्मी सदसत्क्षरमक्षरम् । अविज्ञाता सहस्रांशुर्विधाता कृतलक्षणः ॥** **गभस्तिनेमिः सत्त्वस्थः सिंहो भूतमहेश्वरः । आदिदेवो महादेवो देवेशो देवभृद्गुरुः ॥**

He guards dharma, practises dharma and is full of dharma. The real and the unreal, the perishable and the imperishable, is that God of gods. Not fully known, of a thousand rays, the ordainer who made every sign. He has the wheel of rays, abides in goodness and is lion-like. The great Lord of all beings is that God of gods. The first God, the great God, the lord of the gods and the guru who sustains them.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 51 to 52 mean?
faq.a: He guards dharma, practises dharma and is full of dharma. The real and the unreal, the perishable and the imperishable, is that God of gods. Not fully known, of a thousand rays, the ordainer who made every sign. He has the wheel of rays, abides in goodness and is lion-like. The great Lord of all beings is that God of gods. The first God, the great God, the lord of the gods and the guru who sustains them.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
